commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, the thunderbolt. The second pāda is one of the examples under Prāt. iii. 36.

items.samhita_patha_plain: स स्तनयति स वि द्योतते स उ अश्मानमस्यति ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: स: । स्तनयति । स: । वि । द्योतते । स: । ऊं इति । अश्मानम् । अस्यति ॥७.१३॥

items.samhita_patha: पा॒पाय॑ वा भ॒द्राय॑ वा॒ पुरु॑षा॒यासु॑राय वा ॥

commentaries.whitney: Either for the evil [man] or for the excellent; for man or for Asura.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'For,' i.e. 'at,' ⌊taking the verse as a continuation of 41⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: पापाय वा भद्राय वा पुरुषायासुराय वा ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: पापाय । वा । भद्राय । वा । पुरुषाय । असुराय । वा ॥७.१४॥

items.samhita_patha: यद्वा॑ कृ॒णोष्योष॑धी॒र्यद्वा॑ वर्षसि भ॒द्रया॒ यद्वा॑ ज॒न्यमवी॑वृधः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Either when thou makest the herbs, or when thou rainest excellently, or when thou hast increased him of the people (? janyá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: This appears to be the only example known of the accent janyá instead of jánya , and how little authoritative it is may be inferred from the fact that all our mss. leave avīvṛdhas unaccented after it. Our text makes the necessary emendation to áv- . ⌊All SPP's authorities, however, agree in reading not only janyám but also avīvṛdhas . The latter he also emends to áv- .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: यद्वा कृणोष्योषधीर्यद्वा वर्षसि भद्रया यद्वा जन्यमवीवृधः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यत् । वा । कृणोषि । ओषधी: । यत् । वा । वर्षसि । भद्रया । यत् । वा । जन्यम् । अवीवृध: ॥७.१५॥

items.samhita_patha: तावां॑स्ते मघवन्महि॒मोपो॑ ते त॒न्वः᳡ श॒तम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Such, O bountiful one, is thy greatness; and thine, too ( úpa ), are a hundred bodies.
commentaries.whitney_notes: There is no difficulty in counting the verse into 16 syllables, as required by the Anukr. ⌊It reads naturally as 9 + 8.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: तावांस्ते मघवन्महिमोपो ते तन्वः᳡ शतम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: तावान् । ते । मघऽवन् । महिमा । उपो इति । ते । तन्व᳡: । शतम् ॥७.१६॥

items.samhita_patha: उपो॑ ते॒ बध्वे॒ बद्धा॑नि॒ यदि॒ वासि॒ न्य᳡र्बुदम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thine, too, are two billions, [many] billions (?); or else thou art a hundred million.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies the readings bádve bádvāni , which, on account of the accent, seem probably meant by the mss., which vary between bádhv-, báddh-, báddhv-; K. reads baddhve vádvāni , D. báddhe baddhā́ni . ⌊SPP's authorities also exhibit very wide disagreements, which reflect a corresponding uncertainty of the tradition.⌋ The word is just such a one as the mss. might be expected to boggle and blunder over, both they and we being left without help from the sense. Henry, who accepts the same emendation, understands bádve as locative, which is perhaps better, and at any rate favored by the fact that the pada -text does not read bádve íti .

items.samhita_patha_plain: उपो ते बध्वे बद्धानि यदि वासि न्य᳡र्बुदम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: उपो इति । ते । बध्वे । बध्दानि । यदि । वा । असि । निऽअर्बुदम् ॥७.१७॥

items.samhita_patha: भूया॒निन्द्रो॑ नमु॒राद्भूया॑निन्द्रासि मृ॒त्युभ्यः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: More is Indra than non-dying (??); more art thou, O Indra, than the deaths.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Non-dying' is the conjecture of the Pet. Lexx. for namurá , which occurs nowhere else; it is adopted here, simply for lack of anything better, although in itself of a high degree of implausibility. ⌊Henry also adopts it; but see his note, p. 54.⌋ It is surprising to find Indra brought in here at the end for address, instead of the sun; there is nothing to show that the two remaining paryāyas are not for him. ⌊Note, however, the praise of the sun under the names of Indra and Viṣṇu, so prominent in book xvii., below: see page 805. Perhaps we have here a similar identification.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: भूयानिन्द्रो नमुराद्भूयानिन्द्रासि मृत्युभ्यः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: भूयान् । इन्द्र: । नमुरात् । भूयान् । इन्द्र । असि । मृत्युऽभ्य: ॥८.१॥

items.samhita_patha: भूया॒नरा॑त्याः॒ शच्याः॒ पति॒स्त्वमि॑न्द्रासि वि॒भूः प्र॒भूरिति॒ त्वोपा॑स्महे व॒यम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: More than the niggard, lord of strength ( çácī ) art thou, O Indra; as called mighty, prevailing, do we worship ( upa-ās ) thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Prāt. ii. 71 expressly forbids the combination çácyās p- , which we should have expected here. The verse (9 + 8: 8 = 25) is strangely defined by the Anukr.

items.samhita_patha_plain: भूयानरात्याः शच्याः पतिस्त्वमिन्द्रासि विभूः प्रभूरिति त्वोपास्महे वयम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: भूयान् । अरात्या: । शच्या: । पति: । त्वम् । इन्द्र । असि । विऽभू: । प्रऽभू: । इति । त्वा । उप । आस्महे । वयम् ॥८.२॥

items.samhita_patha: नम॑स्ते अस्तु पश्यत॒ पश्य॑ मा पश्यत ॥

commentaries.whitney: Homage be to thee, O conspicuous one ( paçyata ); see ⌊ páçya ⌋ me, O conspicuous one.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Paçyata is an anomalous and forced substitute for darçata , made in this passage only, for assonance with paçya . The Anukr. ratifies the combination te astu .

items.samhita_patha_plain: नमस्ते अस्तु पश्यत पश्य मा पश्यत ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: नम: । ते । अस्तु । पश्यत । पश्य । मा । पश्यत ॥८.३॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒न्नाद्ये॑न॒ यश॑सा॒ तेज॑सा ब्राह्मणवर्च॒सेन॑ ॥
items.pada_patha: अ॒न्न॒ऽअद्ये॑न । यश॑सा । तेज॑सा । ब्रा॒ह्म॒ण॒ऽव॒र्च॒सेन॑ ॥८.४॥

commentaries.whitney: With food-eating, with glory, with brilliancy ( téjas ), with Brahman-splendor;

items.samhita_patha_plain: अन्नाद्येन यशसा तेजसा ब्राह्मणवर्चसेन ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अन्नऽअद्येन । यशसा । तेजसा । ब्राह्मणऽवर्चसेन ॥८.४॥

items.samhita_patha: अम्भो॒ अमो॒ महः॒ सह॒ इति॒ त्वोपा॑स्महे व॒यम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: As called water (? ámbhas ), force ( áma ), greatness, power, do we worship thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. ratifies the combination ámbho ámo . By a usage that is rare, all the mss. omit in this verse ⌊what follows⌋ after íti , although the repetition is not of the end of the next preceding verse, but of vs. 47. Then, of course, the following verses are written in the same curtailed way until vs. 54, which is filled out to the end.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अम्भो अमो महः सह इति त्वोपास्महे वयम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अम्भ: । अम: । मह: । सह: । इति । त्वा । उप । आस्महे । वयम् ॥८.५॥

items.samhita_patha: अम्भो॑ अरु॒णं र॑ज॒तं रजः॒ सह॒ इति॒ त्वोपा॑स्महे व॒यम् ॥
items.pada_patha: अम्भ॑: । अ॒रु॒णम् । र॒ज॒तम् । रज॑: । सह॑: । इति॑ । त्वा॒ । उप॑ । आ॒स्म॒हे॒ । व॒यम् ॥८.६॥

commentaries.whitney: As called water ( ámbhas ), red, silvery ( rajatá ), welkin ( rájas ), power, do we worship thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Again ⌊as at vs. 31⌋ we have a verse called virāḍ gāyatrī which lacks four syllables of being 24. [ Paryāya VI. — pañca. 52, 53. prājāpatyā ’nuṣṭubh; 54. 2-p. ārṣī gāyatrī. ]

items.samhita_patha_plain: अम्भो अरुणं रजतं रजः सह इति त्वोपास्महे वयम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अम्भ: । अरुणम् । रजतम् । रज: । सह: । इति । त्वा । उप । आस्महे । वयम् ॥८.६॥

items.samhita_patha: उ॒रुः पृ॒थुः सु॒भूर्भुव॒ इति॒ त्वोपा॑स्महे व॒यम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: As called wide, broad, happy ( subhū́ ), earths (? bhúvas ), do we worship thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Bhúvas is here rendered literally, in the only sense which the word has elsewhere in AV. If it is a first appearance of the vyāhṛti common later, its meaning is wholly obscure in this connection. ⌊Aufrecht, KZ. xxxiv. 458, makes some observations about the relations of the noun-forms and adjective-forms in vss. 52-53.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: उरुः पृथुः सुभूर्भुव इति त्वोपास्महे वयम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: उरु: । पृथु: । सुऽभू: । भुव: । इति । त्वा । उप । आस्महे । वयम् ॥९.१॥

items.samhita_patha: प्रथो॒ वरो॒ व्यचो॑ लो॒क इति॒ त्वोपा॑स्महे व॒यम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: As called breadth, width, expanse, world, do we worship thee.

items.samhita_patha_plain: प्रथो वरो व्यचो लोक इति त्वोपास्महे वयम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: प्रथ: । वर: । व्यच: । लोक: । इति । त्वा । उप । आस्महे । वयम् ॥९.२॥

items.samhita_patha: भव॑द्वसुरि॒दद्व॑सुः सं॒यद्व॑सुरा॒यद्व॑सु॒रिति॒ त्वोपा॑स्महे व॒यम् ॥
items.pada_patha: भव॑त्ऽवसु: । इ॒दत्ऽव॑सु: । सं॒यत्ऽव॑सु: । आ॒यत्ऽव॑सु: । इति॑ । त्वा॒ । उप॑ । आ॒स्म॒हे॒ । व॒यम् ॥९.३॥

commentaries.whitney: As called one of arising good, of increasing (??) good, of gathering good, of coming good, do we worship thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies the heroic substitution of vṛdhádvasu for the wholly senseless idádvasu . The Pet. Lexx., to be sure, conjecture for the latter the meaning 'rich in this and that' (which Henry follows); but, besides the fact that idát = idám is not less heroic than idát = vṛdhát , the signification given does not belong rightly to the compound, nor has it any application here. Our rendering has at least concinnity—unless, indeed, in a text of this character, that be an argument against its acceptance. All the compounds are evidently possessive.

items.samhita_patha_plain: भवद्वसुरिदद्वसुः संयद्वसुरायद्वसुरिति त्वोपास्महे वयम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: भवत्ऽवसु: । इदत्ऽवसु: । संयत्ऽवसु: । आयत्ऽवसु: । इति । त्वा । उप । आस्महे । वयम् ॥९.३॥

items.samhita_patha: नम॑स्ते अस्तु पश्यत॒ पश्य॑ मा पश्यत ॥

commentaries.whitney: Homage be to thee, O conspicuous one; see me, O conspicuous one.

items.samhita_patha_plain: नमस्ते अस्तु पश्यत पश्य मा पश्यत ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: नम: । ते । अस्तु । पश्यत । पश्य । मा । पश्यत ॥९.४॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒न्नाद्ये॑न॒ यश॑सा॒ तेज॑सा ब्राह्मणवर्च॒सेन॑ ॥
items.pada_patha: अ॒न्न॒ऽअद्ये॑न । यश॑सा । तेज॑सा । ब्रा॒ह्म॒ण॒ऽव॒र्च॒सेन॑ ॥९.५॥

commentaries.whitney: With food-eating, with glory, with brilliancy, with Brahman-splendor.
commentaries.whitney_notes: These two verses are identical with vss. 48, 49, above ⌊and are therefore not defined by the Anukr.⌋. ⌊The quotations from the Old Anukr., given piecemeal for this paryāya-sūkta at the end of each paryāya , may here be given together: I. trayodaça; II. aṣṭāu ca; III. tataḥ paraḥ sapta; IV. saptadaça; V. ṣaṭ ca bodhyāḥ; VI. ṣaṣṭaḥ pañcaka ucyate. —They are given by SPP. in his "Critical Notice," vol. i., p. 21, with the introductory words, caturthasyā ’vasānāni vakṣyamāṇāni tāni çṛṇu .⌋ ⌊In paryāya V., vss. 47, 50, and 51 have the refrain; and in VI., vss. 52, 53, and 54 have it: these verses are styled gaṇāvasānarcaḥ , and the rest avasānarcaḥ (as was already noted above, p. 472). But since none of the former is divided in two by an avasāna -mark, the distinction does not affect the sums of the " ṛcaḥ of both kinds," which are (as just stated) 3 + 3 for V. and 3 + 2 for VI.⌋ ⌊Here ends the fourth anuvāka , consisting of 1 paryāya-sūkta with 6 paryāyas and 56 verses.⌋ ⌊Some mss. reckon up the hymns as 20 (that is 14 of the decad-divisions of our hymns 1-3, plus 6 paryāyas of our hymn 4) and the verses as 188.⌋ ⌊Here ends the twenty-eighth prapāṭhaka .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: अन्नाद्येन यशसा तेजसा ब्राह्मणवर्चसेन ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अन्नऽअद्येन । यशसा । तेजसा । ब्राह्मणऽवर्चसेन ॥९.५॥
